rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1 line 15 'Access mapping, STRIDE, and the ADR all live here' and chunk 3 line 45 'the test-strategy skill' both resolve against the enclosing module's `## What You'll Learn` (earn-the-trust.md line 23: 'Invoke curated access-control-analysis and STRIDE skills... write the decision as an ADR'; line 25: 'Author a test-strategy skill') via §1's module-include-order carve-out — verified this exercise is the module's FIRST `## Start here` link (earn-the-trust.md line 33, before 'Map the access surface' at line 37, 'Threat-model with STRIDE' at line 39, 'Author your test-strategy skill' at line 41), so this reference draws only on module signposting, never on later sibling exercises. Chunk 4 line 53's 'the test-strategy skill' resolves in-file to chunk 3's own naming (line 45). 'The sibling worktree' (chunk 2 line 33, chunk 3 line 37) resolves back to chunk 1 line 23's definition. No unresolved referent in a fresh read of the current body.

Only cross-file pointer in the body is chunk 1, line 23: 'The [Multi-session and Git survival guide](../trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/multi-session-git.md) carries the longer read.' Named by title, not located by page position — matches the §2 navigational-pointer carve-out. No other file is named anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No 'the X you did/saw/caught' construction anywhere in the body. Verified against earn-the-trust.md line 33: this exercise is the module's first `## Start here` link, so it has no prior in-module beat available to reference.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in the file — this exercise is procedural setup (fork worktree, open second session, arrange windows), no 'take a guess' beat present.

Closest candidate is chunk 2 ('Read back the worktree path', lines 31-34), the file's shortest chunk: 'Claude reports the sibling worktree path. That path is where the second session opens.' Carries one self-standing claim (destination of the next session), not a bare wait-state fragment. The maintainer block (line 57) also carries a direct dated accept-note on exactly this slide: 'Carded and kept (Antti 2026-08-25): the Read back the worktree path slide — the explicit read-back beat stays; do not re-card.'

All four `##` headers are literally true of their chunk content: 'Fork the side worktree from your security lane' (chunk 1) opens the m3-security session and forks via the prompt block; 'Read back the worktree path' (chunk 2) is exactly that beat; 'Open the quality lane in the new worktree' (chunk 3) opens the m3-quality session there; 'Set the two windows side by side' (chunk 4) is the arrangement instruction. None contradicted by chunk body.

Checked all five sub-items against every chunk including the lede. No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction anywhere. No anaphora/epistrophe triples. No self-grading superlative — closest is chunk 0 line 9, 'two Claude Code sessions running side by side on one git history', a plain factual description, not a value claim. No number-with-retraction (the only number in body is '~5 minutes' at line 3, a plain time estimate, never retracted). No abstraction-noun stacks — vocabulary stays concrete throughout (worktree, branch, window, session, skill, path). No verb-triplet construction present to test.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: `sed -n '1,54p' curriculum/exercises/open-the-side-quest.md | grep -n '\*\*'` returns exactly six bolded spans: lines 3/7/9/11 ('Time:', 'What you do:', 'What you build:', 'The point:') and lines 17/39 ('Session' widget labels) — every one a ≤3-word structural chrome label, zero narrative bold anywhere in the body. Corpus check run fresh: `grep -l "^\*\*Time:\*\*" curriculum/exercises/*.md` → 39 files; of those, `grep -l "^\*\*The point:\*\*"` → 29 also carry it — confirms 'The point:' is the same corpus-wide field-label convention as Time:/What you do:/What you build:, not a one-off narrative lead. (The maintainer's own Emphasis note at line 61 is stale — it still names a now-cut 'What happened:' label and omits 'The point:' — but that is a check_writing §3 bookkeeping matter, out of slides scope; the body's actual bold usage stays inside the chrome-label pattern regardless of whether the note describing it is current.)

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All four body headers are imperative ('Fork the side worktree from your security lane', 'Read back the worktree path', 'Open the quality lane in the new worktree', 'Set the two windows side by side') — correct mood for an exercise file; no declarative-claim heading present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 4, line 53, first clause: 'The move this module installs: when one window kicks off a long-running prompt, the other is where you work.' restates chunk 0, line 11: '**The point:** a long-running prompt is dead time only if you have one window.' — same claim, same file, ~40 seconds of read time apart. This is the rule's own named sub-class (c), verbatim shape: 'a koan closing the slide by restating... the exercise's `**The point:**` line.' Harm: the closer spends its one shot at landing something new re-teaching a principle the reader already holds, diluting the genuinely new content in the same bullet's second clause (the concrete main-window/side-window task assignment). All other bullets in the file were checked against all three sub-classes and earn their slot — each states a fact, decision point, or instruction not said elsewhere (worktree definition line 23, CLAUDE.local.md non-sync line 24, base-branch choice line 25, path destination line 33, skill-crossing mechanism line 45). Not blocking: the closer is still fully followable, this is a 'could be tighter' cost, not a comprehension failure.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the first clause of line 53 ('The move this module installs: when one window...you work.'); keep and lead with the second clause ('You run security in the main window from here; the quality side waits until you author the test-strategy skill there.'), which is the only new information.
